newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World jurists body says Tunisia seized lawyer.
newsitem.headline: World jurists body says Tunisia seized lawyer.

text.p: The International Commission of Jurists said on Wednesday a top official of its Tunisian affiliate was arrested on his return from a human rights meeting in Paris.

The respected Geneva-based ICJ, which groups 31 leading judges and lawyers around the globe, said Salah Zeghidi had been seized by Tunisian security officials on Monday at Carthage Airport near Tunis and taken to the Interior Ministry.
"The ICJ fears that Mr Zeghidi could be subjected to maltreatment or torture," declared a statement from the body, which has 75 national sections and affiliated organisations.
Zeghidi is Vice-President of the Tunisian League for the Defence of Human Rights.

The ICJ, which has been increasingly critical of the rights situation in Tunisia over the past year, said it was calling on the Tunisian government "to stop the persecution of human rights defenders."
It also called for Zeghidi's immediate release. The ICJ said it feared his arrest was tied to his presence at a meeting in Paris on October 4 on the rights situation in Tunisia.

In August the ICJ, headed by Senegalese lawyer Adama Dieng, told a United Nations body in Geneva that Tunisians "live under fear and intimidation and several basic rights are flagrantly and systematically violated."
"The use of torture and prolonged illegal detention are widespread," said a statement to the U.N. Sub-Commission on Prevention of Discrimination and Protection of Minorities.
The ICJ, founded in 1952, declares its task is to promote the rule of law throughout the world and work towards full observance of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

Among other targets of its criticism this year have been Israel, the Palestinian Authority, Algeria, Turkey and the United States -- the last for a death penalty system the ICJ says is arbitrary and weighted against blacks.

Earlier this year the ICJ criticised Tunisia over the jailing of opposition member of parliament Khemeis Chammari after he had campaigned for the release of another opposition figure, Mohammed Moada, sentenced to 11 years in prison.
